description: PROTOCOL_SPEC §9.1.1 `extensions.roots` — multi-root discovery WITH namespace isolation (spec v1.46.0, apcore#118 decision D-70). `$defs/ExtensionsConfig`'s own description leads with it: "Supports single root (backward compatible) or multiple roots with namespace isolation." Every entry carries a namespace — auto-derived from the last path segment for a bare string, explicit in the object form — and every SDK already had the scanner that applies it (`scan_multi_root` / `scanMultiRoot`). What was missing differed by SDK, which is why this fixture pins both halves: apcore-python and apcore-typescript read the key at all (a multi-root project worked on one SDK of three, silently), and apcore-rust read the paths and DROPPED the namespaces, so module IDs were unprefixed there and prefixed in the other two. `roots` and `root` are exclusive `oneOf` branches, so a document carrying `roots` is in multi-root mode. Drivers MUST discover from a real directory tree and read the registered module IDs.

test_cases.description: The backward-compatible branch. `extensions.root` prefixes nothing, and wiring `roots` must not change that.
The half apcore-rust honoured only partly: it scanned both roots and prefixed neither.
The other element shape `$defs/ExtensionsConfig` admits. An explicit namespace overrides the derived one.
Nothing in the schema requires a list to be homogeneous, and an operator adding one explicit namespace to a list of paths is the likely way this key is first used.

Namespace isolation is the point of the key, so two roots claiming one namespace is a configuration error rather than a merge. Every SDK's scanner already validated this before scanning anything; until now no configuration could reach the check.

`$defs/ExtensionsConfig` puts them in exclusive `oneOf` branches, so a document carrying both is already outside the schema — but an implementation still has to pick one, and picking `root` would make `roots` inert exactly as it was.

driver_contract.tree: Two sibling trees under the project root, `alpha/executor/svc/mod.<ext>` and `beta/executor/svc/mod.<ext>`, each deriving the unprefixed ID `executor.svc.mod`. Identical IDs on purpose: without namespace prefixing the two collide, which is what makes the prefix observable rather than cosmetic.
driver_contract.discovery: Drivers MUST construct the SDK's registry from a real `apcore.yaml` carrying `input.extensions` and read the registered module IDs after discovery. Calling `scan_multi_root` directly proves the scanner works — which was never the question in any SDK.
